recent_articles.title: Kasaragod district administration prepares railway master plan to end travel hardships - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Kasaragod** district administration has proposed a comprehensive railway master plan to address travel hardships faced by passengers in the northern Kerala region. The proposals, submitted to **Palakkad Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) Madhukar Rawat**, include extending eight trains currently terminating at Kannur and Mangaluru Central/Junction to Kasaragod, as well as restoring discontinued passenger services. The administration also seeks stoppages for three major superfast trains that currently bypass Kasaragod station. These proposals aim to benefit passengers travelling for work, education, medical treatment, pilgrimage, and trade.  The district administration has requested the railway authorities to consider these proposals for improved convenience and efficient travel for residents of Kasaragod.

recent_articles.title: 68% of flyover on Anna Salai completed despite delays due to war, labour shortage - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **State Highways Department** officials report that nearly 68% of the construction project for a flyover on Anna Salai, connecting Saidapet and Teynampet, has been completed.  The project is expected to be finished by September with 32 out of 131 decks in place. The completion of the flyover will involve placing slabs on girders, completing foundation work for pillars, and installing approach ramps and crash barriers.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders demanded the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the **Union Education Minister**, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. **Rahul Gandhi** called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court closes plea of Goa Congress leader after his death from snakebite - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** closed the plea of deceased **Ketan Bhatikar**, a Congress candidate for the Ponda Assembly seat, challenging a Bombay High Court order cancelling the bypoll.  Bhatikar died from a snakebite on Thursday and his lawyer requested the court to leave the larger question of law open while closing the proceedings. The High Court had earlier canceled the bypoll citing violation of the Representation of the People Act as less than one year remained in the term of the Assembly.

recent_articles.title: Sebi approves IPO plans of Neolite Lightings, Aspri Spirits and SS Retail - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Neolite ZKW Lightings**, a manufacturer of automotive lighting products, plans to raise Rs 600 crore through a combination of fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will be used for setting up a greenfield manufacturing facility in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, expanding existing operations, and repaying borrowings. **Neolite ZKW Lightings** has a significant market share in India's commercial vehicle lighting segment and serves over 40 OEM customers. Meanwhile, **Aspri Spirits**, an importer and distributor of international wine and spirits, received Sebi approval for its public issue with a proposed IPO of up to Rs 140 crore.  SS Retail, another company seeking regulatory clearance, plans to raise Rs 500 crore through its IPO, which will be used for expansion and growth.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Governor’s role in government formation | Explained - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** secured a majority in the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, but the Governor invited the party's chief to form the government.  **C. Joseph Vijay**, the TVK leader, was sworn in as Chief Minister after securing letters of support from 120 members. The Governor's discretion in appointing the Chief Minister is based on constitutional provisions and previous recommendations by commissions, but there have been instances where Governors have appointed a Chief Minister without following these guidelines.  The Supreme Court has emphasized that the "floor of the House" is the appropriate forum to determine majority support for a government.

recent_articles.title: PM Modi assures more support to Telangana, asks CM Revanth to collaborate with him - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** assured **Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy** that the **Central government** would continue to support its development, emphasizing the importance of state-level progress for a developed India by 2047.  During his visit on May 10, 2026, **Modi** inaugurated several developmental projects worth ₹9,400 crore, including industrial parks and railway infrastructure, aiming to make Telangana a manufacturing hub. He highlighted the government's commitment to creating employment opportunities and reviving the textile industry through schemes like PM Mitra Park at Warangal and investments in infrastructure development.  The Prime Minister also emphasized the importance of energy security with the launch of the Malkapur terminal.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: Urrak: Goa’s liquid summer soul - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Goans** have a deep connection to the cashew tree, which is integral to their culture and agriculture. The tree's adaptability to infertile soil and its strong roots make it ideal for coastal planting, providing protection for farmlands in the interior.  The fruit is fermented into **urrak**, an alcoholic beverage that is considered a symbol of Goa's traditional spirit and a key element of summer celebrations.  **Urrak** production relies on ancient techniques like foot-crushing to extract juice, emphasizing sustainability and community involvement. The unique flavor profile of **urrak** makes it distinct from mass-produced spirits and is enjoyed by locals in their homes, often accompanied by local cuisine.

recent_articles.title: Urrak: How the jungle juice from Goa is having its moment - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Urrak**, a cashew-based spirit, has experienced a surge in popularity in Goa, becoming the state's official summer drink.  Its accessibility and refreshing taste have contributed to its widespread appeal, with **Mac Vaz**, founder of the All Goa Cashew Feni Distillers & Bottlers Association, noting that it is "deceptively smooth" and hangover-free. The spirit has also garnered attention from mixologists who are experimenting with new cocktails featuring urrak, further boosting its popularity.  **Deviya Rane**, MLA and chairperson of the Goa Forest Development Corporation, recognizes the cultural significance of urrak and supports efforts to elevate it to a premium status globally through initiatives like the Cashew Fest.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Two highway defects in Karnataka over three years: Debarment, repairs ordered - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **National Highways (NHs)** in Karnataka have experienced two major incidents of structural defects and collapses over the past three years.  In 2025, a reinforced earth wall block collapsed on NH-948, prompting repair work based on recommendations from **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)** experts. In 2024, the Kali Bridge on NH-66 collapsed due to inadequate slope stability works, leading to the contractor's one-month debarment and corrective measures.  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has taken action against defaulting agencies based on severity of violations, including penalties, contract termination, or blacklisting.

recent_articles.title: Meta sets up automatic blocking for govt., police-referred content - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Meta**, the parent company of **Facebook** and **Instagram**, has been complying with censorship orders from Indian authorities, restricting content on its platforms based on local laws. The Sahyog portal, used by police to request takedowns, allows for immediate restriction of access without requiring a formal legal process.  The firm's response is to instantly remove content flagged through this mechanism, even after determining the takedown may be legally improper. Critics argue that this practice creates an "infrastructure of censorship" and undermines free speech, while experts call on **Meta** to publish all takedown notices and challenge frivolous ones in court.

recent_articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Girotra**, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  **Ashok Sengupta**, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. **Isaac Kehimkar**, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Government** celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

recent_articles.title: Pakistan out of women’s football tournament in India over political strife | Football News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pakistan**'s women's football team will not participate in the **South Asian Football Federation (SAFF)** Women’s Championship hosted in India due to ongoing geopolitical tensions between the two nations. The Pakistani government has barred the team from traveling, citing a lack of an NOC from relevant authorities.  The tournament is scheduled for May 25 to June 7 and will be held at Goa's Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. This decision follows a long history of strained relations between India and **Pakistan**, which have impacted cross-border travel for athletes in various sports, including cricket.
